correctness.rationale: Arbitrary antiderivative tests in the real voltage coordinate give \(\mathbb E[\sin\phi\mid v]=I-\gamma v\). The periodic test \(\cos\phi\) gives \(\mathbb E[v\sin\phi]=0\), and combining the two yields \(\gamma\mathbb E[v^2]=I\mathbb E[v]\) and the exact variance parabola. The acceleration is the conditional-regression residual, so orthogonality gives the exact sine-current variance defect and covariance. Zero mean or zero residual energy forces invariant support onto the Josephson equilibria. For \(I>1\), strict residual energy together with \(|\sin\phi|\le1\) yields the strict lower mean-voltage floor. The packaged checker verifies all algebraic reductions with exact arithmetic.

value.rationale: The instantaneous velocity is the normalized junction voltage and its stationary mean is the central dc observable in Josephson current-voltage theory, so the accepted quantity is physically intrinsic rather than an arbitrary moment. The theorem identifies the entire conditional mean of the Josephson sine current at fixed voltage, converts it into an exact voltage-variance parabola, and measures the failure of perfect regression by mean-square acceleration. Above the critical bias it yields a parameter-only strict lower bound on every compact stationary mean voltage, independent of the particular running branch. These identities provide exact consistency checks for autonomous running-state computations and separate equilibrium-supported states sharply from genuinely moving recurrent statistics.
